title: Spinach & Cheddar Omelette
steps: Shred the cheddar if it is not already grated, roughly chop the 1 cup of spinach, and set both next to the stove so everything is ready once the eggs hit the pan.
Crack the 3 eggs into a bowl, add a pinch of salt, and whisk with a fork for about 30 seconds until the yolks and whites are fully blended with no streaks.
Melt 1/2 tablespoon of the butter in a 8-inch nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the spinach and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until just wilted, then tip it onto a plate.

Return the pan to medium-low heat and melt the remaining butter until it foams. Pour in the eggs and let them sit for 15 seconds, then drag the edges toward the center with a spatula, tilting the pan so the raw egg runs underneath.
When the top is mostly set but still a little glossy, about 2 minutes, scatter the spinach and cheddar over one half of the omelette.
Fold the empty half over the filling, cook 30 seconds more so the cheese melts, then slide onto a plate and serve right away.

title: Classic Scrambled Eggs on Toast
steps: Crack the 4 eggs into a bowl, add a pinch each of salt and pepper, and whisk well for about 30 seconds until completely smooth and slightly frothy.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over low heat until it just begins to foam, without letting it brown.
Pour in the eggs and let them sit for about 20 seconds until the edges barely start to set. Then stir slowly with a spatula, pushing the curds from the edges to the center.

Keep stirring gently for 3 to 4 minutes, lifting the pan off the heat for a few seconds if it gets too hot. Stop when the eggs look soft, creamy, and just set but still a little wet, since they will keep cooking.
Toast the 2 slices of bread while the eggs cook, until golden brown and crisp at the edges.
Pile the eggs onto the hot toast, finish with another pinch of pepper, and eat immediately.

title: Egg Fried Rice
steps: Slice the 2 green onion stalks thinly, keeping the white and green parts separate. Break up any clumps in the 2 cups of cooked rice with your fingers, since cold, dry rice fries best.
Beat the 2 eggs with a pinch of salt in a small bowl until the yolks are fully broken up.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the white parts of the green onion and stir for 15 seconds until fragrant.
Push the onion to one side, pour in the eggs, and stir gently for 30 to 45 seconds until they are softly scrambled and just set. Break them into small pieces.
Add the rice and spread it across the pan. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing occasionally, until the grains are hot and a few start to turn lightly golden.
Drizzle the soy sauce around the edges of the pan and toss for 30 seconds until the rice is evenly coloured. Stir in the green parts of the onion and serve hot.

title: Veggie Fried Rice
steps: Mince the 2 garlic cloves and break up any clumps in the 2 cups of cooked rice. Beat the 2 eggs with a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the garlic and stir for 20 to 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the 1 cup of frozen vegetables straight from the freezer and cook, stirring often, for 3 to 4 minutes until thawed, hot, and any extra moisture has cooked off.
Push the vegetables to one side and pour the eggs into the cleared space. Stir for about 30 seconds until just set, then mix them into the vegetables.
Add the rice and spread it out. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing occasionally, until steaming and starting to crisp in spots.
Pour the soy sauce around the edge of the pan, toss everything for 30 seconds until evenly coated, and taste for salt and pepper before serving.

title: Garlic Butter Pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and stir in 1 teaspoon of salt. Meanwhile, mince the 4 garlic cloves finely and grate the parmesan if needed.
Add the 8 oz of pasta and cook, stirring occasionally, for 1 to 2 minutes less than the package time, until just al dente with a slight bite at the center.
Before draining, scoop out about 1/2 cup of the starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta.
In the same pot, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook for 45 to 60 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant and pale gold. Do not let it brown or it will turn bitter.
Add the pasta back with a splash of the pasta water and toss for 1 minute so the butter and water cling to the noodles in a glossy sauce.
Take the pot off the heat, add the parmesan, and toss until melted and smooth, adding more pasta water a tablespoon at a time if it looks dry. Finish with pepper and serve hot.

title: Tomato Basil Spaghetti
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 teaspoon of salt. Thinly slice the 3 garlic cloves and tear the basil leaves by hand, saving a few for garnish.
Warm the olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant and barely golden.

Pour in the can of tomatoes, crushing them with the back of a spoon, and add a pinch of pepper. Simmer over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and darkens slightly.
While the sauce simmers, cook the 8 oz of spaghetti in the boiling water until al dente, usually 8 to 10 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water before draining.
Add the drained spaghetti to the skillet and toss over medium heat for 1 minute, adding a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too thick, until every strand is coated.
Stir in most of the basil, taste for salt, and serve topped with the reserved leaves.

title: Pesto Pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Halve the 1 cup of cherry tomatoes and grate the parmesan if needed.
Cook the 8 oz of pasta until al dente, following the package time, usually 9 to 11 minutes. Scoop out about 1/2 cup of the pasta water before draining.
Return the drained pasta to the warm pot off the heat. Add the pesto and a few tablespoons of pasta water and toss until the noodles are evenly coated and the sauce looks creamy rather than oily.
Fold in the cherry tomatoes and toss for 30 seconds so they warm through without breaking down.
Stir in half the parmesan and loosen with more pasta water if needed. Taste for salt and pepper, then serve topped with the remaining parmesan.

title: Creamy Mushroom Pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them about 1/4 inch thick, mince the 3 garlic cloves, and grate the parmesan.
Cook the 8 oz of pasta until al dente, usually 9 to 11 minutes. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

While the pasta cooks, melt the butter with a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and cook, stirring only occasionally, for 6 to 8 minutes until the liquid has evaporated and they are deeply golden. Season with salt and pepper.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic, and stir for 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the 3/4 cup of heavy cream and simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Add the pasta and parmesan to the skillet and toss for 1 minute, loosening with pasta water as needed, until the sauce is silky and clings to every piece. Serve immediately.

title: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
steps: Shred the 1 1/2 cups of cheddar yourself if you can, since freshly shredded melts more smoothly than pre-shredded. Bring a pot of water to a boil with 1 teaspoon of salt.
Cook the 8 oz of macaroni for 1 minute less than the package directs, usually 6 to 7 minutes, until tender but still firm. Drain, but do not rinse.
Return the empty pot to low heat and melt the butter. Pour in the 3/4 cup of milk and warm it for 1 to 2 minutes until steaming but not boiling.
Add the macaroni back to the pot and stir for 1 minute so it absorbs some of the milk and the sauce begins to thicken slightly.
Take the pot off the heat, add the cheddar a handful at a time, and stir until each addition has melted before adding the next, giving a smooth, glossy sauce.
Season with pepper and more salt to taste. Let it rest for 2 minutes to thicken, then serve hot.

title: Chicken & Broccoli Stir-Fry
steps: Slice the 1 lb of chicken breast across the grain into thin strips about 1/4 inch thick, and pat dry with paper towels. Cut the broccoli into bite-size florets and mince the 3 garlic cloves.
Toss the chicken with a pinch each of salt and pepper and 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, and let it sit while the pan heats.

Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until it just begins to smoke. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through with no pink in the center. Transfer to a plate.
Add the broccoli and 2 tablespoons of water to the same pan, cover, and steam for 2 to 3 minutes until bright green and just tender-crisp.
Uncover, add the garlic, and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Return the chicken to the pan and pour in the remaining 2 tablespoons of soy sauce.
Toss everything for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce coats the chicken and slightly reduces. Serve over the 2 cups of warm cooked rice.

title: Lemon Garlic Chicken
steps: Pat the chicken breasts dry and, if they are thick, slice each in half horizontally so they cook evenly at about 1/2 inch thick. Mince the 4 garlic cloves and juice the lemon.
Season both sides generously with the salt and pepper.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the butter with a drizzle of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until foaming. Add the chicken and cook undisturbed for 5 to 6 minutes until deeply golden on the bottom.
Flip, reduce the heat to medium, and cook another 4 to 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside and the juices run clear. Move it to a plate and cover loosely.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, add the remaining butter and the garlic, and stir for 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the lemon juice and scrape up the browned bits from the pan.
Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce is slightly thickened, return the chicken to the pan, and spoon the sauce over the top before serving.

title: Chicken Quesadillas
steps: Pull or chop the 2 cups of rotisserie chicken into small bite-size pieces, discarding any skin or bones, and make sure the cheddar is shredded.
Lay the 4 tortillas on a clean surface. Sprinkle one half of each with about 1/4 cup cheddar, then top with chicken and a spoonful of salsa.
Cover with a final sprinkle of cheese, which helps glue the filling together, and fold each tortilla in half.
Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat. Cook 1 or 2 quesadillas at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until the underside is golden brown and crisp.
Flip carefully and cook another 2 minutes until the second side is golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Rest on a cutting board for 1 minute, slice into wedges, and serve with extra salsa.

title: Cheese Quesadilla
steps: Shred the 1 cup of cheddar if needed. Lay the 2 tortillas flat on a clean surface.
Sprinkle the cheese evenly over one half of each tortilla, leaving a small border at the edge, and spoon the salsa over the cheese if you want it inside.
Fold each tortilla in half and press down gently.
Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat. Place the quesadillas in the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the bottom is golden brown with a few darker spots.
Flip and cook for another 2 minutes until the cheese has melted completely and the second side is crisp. Slice into wedges and serve with the rest of the salsa for dipping.

title: Black Bean Tacos
steps: Drain and rinse the can of black beans in a colander until the water runs clear. Halve and pit the avocado, scoop it into a bowl, and cut the lime into wedges.
Warm a small saucepan over medium heat and add a drizzle of oil. Add the beans, 1 teaspoon of cumin, a pinch of salt, and 2 tablespoons of water.
Simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring and mashing about a quarter of the beans with a spoon, until the mixture is thick and fragrant.
Mash the avocado with a fork, squeeze in the juice of half the lime, and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat and warm each of the 6 tortillas for 20 to 30 seconds per side until soft and lightly charred in spots.
Fill each tortilla with beans, a spoonful of avocado, and salsa, then serve with the remaining lime wedges for squeezing over.

title: Beef Tacos
steps: Shred the lettuce into thin ribbons and make sure the cheddar is shredded. Set both aside in separate bowls.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the 1 lb of ground beef and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles with a wooden spoon, until fully browned with no pink remaining. Spoon off any excess fat.

Sprinkle in the 2 tablespoons of taco seasoning and add 1/4 cup of water. Simmer over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the liquid has mostly reduced and the beef is coated in a thick sauce.
Warm each of the 8 tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high heat for about 20 seconds per side until pliable and lightly toasted.
Fill each tortilla with a generous spoonful of beef, then top with the cheddar and shredded lettuce. Serve right away while the beef is hot.

title: Tuna Melt
steps: Drain the can of tuna very well, pressing out the liquid, and flake it into a bowl. Stir in the 2 tablespoons of mayonnaise and a pinch each of salt and pepper until combined.
Divide the tuna mixture between 2 slices of bread, spreading it to the edges, and top each with a slice of cheddar. Close the sandwiches with the other 2 slices.

Heat a large skillet over medium-low heat and add a little oil. Cook the sandwiches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing lightly, until the bread is deeply golden and the cheese has melted. Slice in half and serve hot.

title: Grilled Cheese & Tomato
steps: Slice the tomato into 1/4-inch rounds and pat them dry with paper towels so the sandwich does not get soggy. Spread the butter on one side of each of the 4 bread slices.

Place 2 slices butter side down in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Top each with a slice of cheddar, a layer of tomato, a pinch of salt and pepper, and another slice of cheddar, then close with the remaining bread, butter side up.

Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the bottom is golden brown, then flip and cook another 3 minutes, pressing gently, until the cheese is fully melted and the second side is crisp. Rest for 1 minute, then slice and serve.

title: Avocado Toast with Egg
steps: Halve and pit the avocado, scoop the flesh into a bowl, and mash it with a fork leaving some small chunks. Squeeze in the juice of the lemon half and season with salt and pepper.
Toast the 2 bread slices until golden brown and firm enough to hold the toppings.

Heat a nonstick skillet with a little oil over medium heat. Crack in the 2 eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set and opaque but the yolks are still runny. For a firmer yolk, flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Spread the avocado generously over each slice of toast, then slide an egg on top. Finish with a pinch of salt and pepper and eat immediately.

title: Caprese Salad
steps: Take the mozzarella out of its liquid, pat it dry with paper towels, and let it come close to room temperature for about 10 minutes for better flavor.
Slice the 2 tomatoes and the 8 oz of mozzarella into 1/4-inch rounds, discarding the end pieces of tomato if they are tough.
Arrange the tomato and mozzarella on a platter, alternating and slightly overlapping them, and tuck whole basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle with the olive oil, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and some pepper, and serve right away while the tomatoes are cool and the cheese is soft.

title: Greek Salad
steps: Cut the cucumber into 1/2-inch chunks, quarter or slice the 2 tomatoes into bite-size wedges, and slice the 1/4 red onion as thinly as you can. Soak the onion in cold water for 5 minutes to soften its bite, then drain well.
Place the cucumber, tomatoes, and drained onion in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil, oregano, a pinch of salt, and a little pepper, and toss gently for 30 seconds until everything is lightly coated.
Crumble the 1/2 cup of feta over the top in large pieces and serve right away, or chill for 10 minutes to let the flavors blend.

title: Chickpea Curry
steps: Finely dice the onion and mince the 3 garlic cloves. Drain and rinse the can of chickpeas in a colander.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent with golden edges.
Stir in the garlic and the 2 tablespoons of curry powder and cook for 1 minute until very fragrant, adding a splash of water if it starts to stick.
Add the chickpeas and the can of coconut milk, scraping up anything stuck to the bottom. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, uncovered, for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and creamy and clings to the chickpeas. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve spooned over the 2 cups of warm cooked rice.

title: Lentil Soup
steps: Rinse the 1 cup of lentils in a fine strainer and pick out any debris. Dice the onion, carrots, and celery into small 1/4-inch pieces so they cook evenly.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery with a pinch of salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until softened and the onion is translucent.
Stir in the 1 teaspoon of cumin and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lentils, the 4 cups of broth, and 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cover partially and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are completely tender and the soup has thickened. Add more water if it becomes too thick.
Taste and adjust with salt and pepper. For a creamier texture, mash some of the soup against the side of the pot with a spoon before serving.

title: Tomato Soup
steps: Roughly chop the onion and mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Heat a drizzle of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 to 45 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the can of tomatoes, including the juices, and the 2 cups of broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, partially covered, for 20 minutes until the onion is completely tender and the flavors have blended.
Blend the soup until completely smooth, using an immersion blender or by working in batches in a regular blender with the lid vented to let steam escape.
Return to low heat, stir in the 1/2 cup of cream, and warm for 2 minutes without boiling. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Roasted Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and place a rimmed baking sheet inside while it heats. Scrub the potatoes and cut them into 1-inch chunks so they cook at the same rate.
Pat the potatoes dry with a clean towel, then toss in a large bowl with the olive oil, the salt, and a few grinds of pepper until every piece is glossy.
Carefully pull out the hot baking sheet and spread the potatoes in a single layer, cut sides down, without crowding. Roast for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, smash the garlic cloves lightly with the flat of a knife and strip the rosemary leaves from the sprigs.
Flip the potatoes, scatter the garlic and rosemary over the top, and roast for 15 to 20 minutes more until the outsides are deep golden and crisp and a fork slides easily into the centers.
Taste for salt and serve hot straight from the pan.

title: Sheet Pan Sausage & Veggies
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Cut the sausage into 1-inch pieces, slice the 2 bell peppers and the onion into 1-inch strips, and cut the potatoes into 3/4-inch cubes, since potatoes take the longest.
On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss the potatoes with half the olive oil, half the paprika, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread them out and roast for 10 minutes.
In a bowl, toss the peppers and onion with the remaining olive oil and paprika and a pinch of salt.
Remove the pan, add the vegetables and sausage, and stir to combine, spreading everything in a single layer with some space between the pieces so it roasts rather than steams.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the potatoes are tender and golden, the vegetables have charred edges, and the sausage is browned and cooked through.
Let it rest for 2 minutes, then serve directly from the pan.

title: Honey Garlic Salmon
steps: Take the salmon out of the fridge 10 minutes ahead, pat the fillets dry, and season both sides with salt and pepper. Mince the 3 garlic cloves and juice the 1/2 lemon.
Whisk the 2 tablespoons of honey, 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, garlic, and lemon juice together in a small bowl until smooth.

Heat a drizzle of oil in a large nonstick or oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Place the fillets in the pan skin side up and sear undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden.

Flip the fillets, reduce the heat to medium-low, and pour in the sauce. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, spooning the sauce over the fish, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and the sauce is thick and syrupy.
Transfer to plates, spoon the pan sauce over the top, and serve immediately.

title: Garlic Shrimp
steps: Peel the shrimp if needed, devein them, and pat completely dry with paper towels so they sear instead of steam. Season with salt and pepper. Mince the 4 garlic cloves, chop the parsley, and juice the 1/2 lemon.
Heat a drizzle of oil with 1 tablespoon of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat until foaming.
Add the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes without moving until pink and lightly golden on the bottom. Flip and cook 1 minute more, then transfer to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining butter and the garlic, and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Return the shrimp, add the lemon juice, and toss for 30 seconds until coated. Sprinkle with parsley and serve right away.

title: Tofu Teriyaki Bowl
steps: Drain the tofu, wrap it in a clean towel, and press under a heavy pan for 15 minutes to remove excess water. Cut it into 3/4-inch cubes and cut the broccoli into small florets.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until golden and crisp on most sides.
Move the tofu to one side, add the broccoli and 3 tablespoons of water, cover, and steam for 3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Uncover and pour in the 1/4 cup of teriyaki sauce. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat until the sauce bubbles, thickens, and glazes the tofu and broccoli.
Divide the 2 cups of warm cooked rice between bowls, top with the tofu and broccoli, and spoon any extra sauce from the pan over the top.

title: Banana Pancakes
steps: Peel the ripe banana and mash it in a large bowl with a fork until mostly smooth with a few small lumps. Whisk in the egg and the 1/3 cup of milk until well combined.
Add the 1/2 cup of flour and a pinch of salt and stir just until no dry streaks remain. A few small lumps are fine, and overmixing makes tough pancakes. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes, then melt a little of the butter in the pan, swirling to coat.
Pour in about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set and dry.
Flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes more until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding butter as needed, and serve warm.

title: Yogurt Parfait
steps: Rinse the 1/2 cup of blueberries and pat them dry. Choose a tall glass or jar so you can see the layers.
Spoon about 1/3 cup of the yogurt into the bottom of the glass, then add a layer of granola and a scattering of blueberries.
Repeat the layers with the remaining yogurt, granola, and blueberries, finishing with a generous layer of berries on top.
Drizzle the 1 tablespoon of honey over the top and serve right away so the granola stays crunchy.

title: Peanut Butter Banana Toast
steps: Peel the banana and slice it into rounds about 1/4 inch thick.
Toast the 2 slices of bread until deep golden brown and crisp, about 2 to 3 minutes, so they can hold up to the toppings.

While the toast is still warm, spread 1 tablespoon of peanut butter on each slice all the way to the edges so it softens slightly. Arrange the banana rounds on top in an overlapping layer, drizzle with the honey, and eat right away.
